question: Which of the following antitumor agents acts forming a covalent and irreversible complex with the thymidylate synthase and its cofactor, previous activation to the corresponding deoxynucleotide?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Thymidylate synthase" -> "involved in DNA synthesis" -> "requires cofactor for activity" -> "5-Fluorouracil forms covalent bond" -> "inhibits thymidylate synthase" -> "prevents DNA synthesis" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Methotrexate" -> "inhibits dihydrofolate reductase" -> "reduces folate availability" -> "affects nucleotide synthesis" -> "does not form covalent bond with thymidylate synthase" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Bortezomib" -> "inhibits proteasome" -> "affects protein degradation" -> "not directly related to thymidylate synthase" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Cyclophosphamide" -> "alkylating agent" -> "cross-links DNA" -> "not specific to thymidylate synthase" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Taxol" -> "stabilizes microtubules" -> "affects mitosis" -> "not related to thymidylate synthase" -> 50%
analysis: 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) is an antitumor agent that acts by forming a covalent and irreversible complex with thymidylate synthase, which is essential for DNA synthesis. It is activated to its corresponding deoxynucleotide form, which then inhibits the enzyme, leading to decreased thymidine production and ultimately affecting DNA replication and cell division.
